This page is for people who build or support models in [Atomica](https://atomica.tools): a framework workbook of compartments, parameters, and a transition matrix, a databook of values by population and year, a program book of spending, unit costs, and effects, and calibration, scenarios, and budget optimization. It shows an Atomica model next to the same model in Starsim, how their results agree, how long each takes, and what works and what does not yet, including what fails. Starsim is a Python library: it reads Atomica's workbooks, but it has no spreadsheet interface or user interface of its own for analysts who do not program.

## The same model in both

Atomica's SIR demo, in its framework workbook (shown here as CSV, one sheet at a time) and its databook. The compartments:

```
Code Name,Display Name,Is Source,Is Sink,Is Junction,Databook Page,Databook Order,Setup Weight
sus,Susceptible,n,n,n,state_variables,,
inf,Infected,n,n,n,,,
rec,Recovered,n,n,n,,,
dead,Dead,n,y,n,,,
```

The parameters, with the force of infection as a function of them:

```
Code Name,Display Name,Format,Databook Page,Targetable,Databook Order,Default Value,Function
transpercontact,Transmission probability per contact,Probability,parameters,y,,0.0008,
contacts,Number of contacts annually,,parameters,y,,80,
recrate,Average duration of infections (years),Duration,parameters,y,,0.5,
infdeath,Death rate for infected people,Rate,parameters,y,,0.016,
susdeath,Death rate for susceptible people,Rate,parameters,y,,0.008,
foi,Force of infection,Rate,,,,,(1 - (1-ch_prev*transpercontact)**floor(contacts)*(1-ch_prev*transpercontact*(contacts-floor(contacts))))*(1-susdeath)
```

The transition matrix:

```
,sus,inf,rec,dead
sus,,foi,,susdeath
inf,,,recrate,"susdeath,infdeath"
rec,,,,susdeath
dead,,,,
```

The framework also has eight characteristics (such as prevalence, `ch_prev = inf/ch_all`) and a cascade, and the databook gives the values (a transmission probability of 0.008, 80 contacts a year, infections lasting 5 years, and so on) and the initial numbers. Atomica takes one Euler step a year here.

In Starsim, the compartments are states, each parameter is an `ss.par`, and each cell of the transition matrix is a transition. `integrator='euler', substeps=1` steps the model as Atomica does:

```{python}
import starsim as ss

transpercontact = ss.par(0.008, doc='Transmission probability per contact')
contacts        = ss.par(80,    doc='Number of contacts annually')
susdeath        = ss.par(ss.peryear(0.008), doc='Death rate for susceptible people')
infdeath        = ss.par(ss.peryear(0.016), doc='Death rate for infected people, in addition')

sus, inf, rec, dead = ss.states(4)
prev = inf.n / (sus + inf + rec).n
foi  = (1 - (1 - prev * transpercontact)**contacts) * (1 - 0.008)

sir = ss.Disease(
    infection  = sus >> inf @ foi,
    recovery   = inf >> rec @ ss.years(5),
    death      = sus + inf + rec >> dead @ susdeath,
    inf_death  = inf >> dead @ infdeath,
    init_n     = dict(sus=700, inf=285.71429, rec=14.28571),
    first      = 'sus',
)
sim = ss.Sim(sir, total_pop=1000, start=2000, stop=2023, integrator='euler', substeps=1, verbose=0) # Atomica takes one Euler step a year
sim.run()
sim.plot()
```

Or the workbooks can be imported as they are:

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| label: starsim-import
sim = ss.import_from('sir_framework.xlsx', format='atomica', databook='sir_databook.xlsx', dt=1, start=2000, stop=2023)
sim.run()
```

## How the results agree

| Model | Agreement |
|---|---|
| The SIR demo (above) | Identical: every compartment, to rounding error |
| The HIV demo (a cascade by sex, 7 programs, 3 budgets), written by hand | Identical: a largest difference of 2 in 10<sup>14</sup>, in every compartment and every level of the cascade of both sexes, without programs and with the default, doubled, and zero budgets |
| Atomica's library workbooks, imported with `ss.import_from()` | `sir`, `hiv_dyn`, `sir_vaccine`, and `udt` agree with Atomica 1.32.4's own runs to within 1e-9 (checked by the switching demo). The review that the demo is built from found 9 of Atomica's 16 library demos imported and agreed to 1e-12 or better. `tb` fails today (below) |

## Timings

Lines are lines of model code (not counting blank lines, comments, imports, or plotting, and counting a line over 100 characters twice), against the rows of Atomica's spreadsheets plus its Python; times are for one run. Both are measured by Starsim's north-star script, `tests/north_star/north_star.py` in the lingua_franca_design repo (see the [index page](../library_landscape.qmd#how-these-numbers-were-made)). Atomica 1.32.4's times were recorded on the same machine, for `Project.run_sim()` with the spreadsheets already loaded.

| Model | Lines: Atomica | Lines: Starsim | One run: Atomica | One run: Starsim | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The SIR demo | 62 (59 spreadsheet rows, 3 lines of Python) | 16 | 0.0025 s | 0.016 s to build and run (0.07 s the first time in a new process); 0.5 ms to rerun a built sim | Pass |
| The HIV demo | 217 (188 spreadsheet rows, 29 lines of Python) | 67 | 0.0047 to 0.0054 s | 0.11 s (0.16 s the first time) | Pass |
| Budget optimization of the HIV demo over its 7 programs | | | 1.3 s | 2.3 s | |

A spreadsheet row that a program officer fills in is not the same as a line of Python, so the line counts compare unlike things. The first time Starsim runs after it is installed, its compiled code is compiled, which takes up to half a minute; this happens once.

## What works and what does not yet

These are from Starsim's switching demo for Atomica users (`tests/switching/test_atomica.py` in the lingua_franca_design repo), which checks each task against Atomica's numbers, and from the review it was built from. "Fails" means the demo's check does not pass today.

| Task | Today |
|---|---|
| Import a framework and databook from Atomica's library (`sir`, `hiv_dyn`, `sir_vaccine`, `udt`) | **Works**: agreement to within 1e-9; the timed vaccine duration of `sir_vaccine` is a fixed dwell time |
| Import `tb`, Atomica's flagship TB demo | **Fails**: it imports, but lists 81 parts as not translated (junctions, references to flows such as `life_expectancy*:ddis`, `SRC_POP_AVG()`, and interactions), and the run stops when a compartment stops being a number |
| Calibrate an imported workbook to its databook's data | **Works**: bounds on two parameters (`sim.new(pars=dict(transpercontact=ss.par(0.008, bounds=[0.0008, 0.024]), ...))`) and `sim.fit(data=...)`; the mean error is 0.01% of the data, against 4.5% for Atomica's own calibration of the same demo |
| Import a program book and optimize the budget: reallocate the HIV demo's $164 million across its seven programs to maximize the number virally suppressed in 2030 | **Works**: `ss.import_from(..., progbook='hiv_dyn_progbook.xlsx', programs_start=2020)` gives Atomica's baseline exactly, and `ss.fit.optimize(sim, total=..., start=2020, maximize='all_vs', at=2030)` finds 1,066,910 suppressed, against 1,067,056 for Atomica's optimizer (from 374,830 at the current allocation), in 2.3 s against 1.3 s |
| The least money that reaches a target, with limits by program (Atomica's money minimization) | **Works**: `ss.fit.optimize(sim, start=2020, maximize='all_vs', at=2030, target=1e6, bounds=dict(...))`; on the HIV demo, a million virally suppressed in 2030 needs $133 million, in 5.5 s |
| Programs declared for a model written by hand (spending to coverage to effect) | **Not yet**: the importer writes programs as expressions; there is no `ss.program()` |
| A databook generated from the model and read back | **Not yet** |
| Costs of deliveries, by population | **Works**: products have `cost=`, and deliveries report `delivered`, `coverage`, and `cost` |
| The same model with chance, for a small province | **Works**: `solver='binomial'` |
| A user interface for analysts who do not program | **Not planned** |

## Bringing your model in

`ss.import_from('framework.xlsx', format='atomica', databook='databook.xlsx')` reads an Atomica framework and databook, and `progbook=` adds a program book. Compartments become states, characteristics become results, and each parameter on the transition matrix a transition; parameters with functions become expressions of the counts. Atomica moves `value × dt` of a compartment each step for a rate or probability, `dt/value` for a duration, and `value × dt` people for a number, which is the Euler step, so the sim is stepped as Atomica steps it. Several populations become a stratification by population, and a program book's programs become parameters of spending, whose coverage changes the parameters they affect. Junctions, transfers, and interactions are not translated; what is not translated is listed (`sim.imported.incomplete`), and `sim.imported.prompt` is a prompt for an AI assistant with Starsim's import-model skill to finish the job. The import is Starsim code, kept as `sim.imported.code`, to save and change as a Python file.

See [Import/export](index.qmd) for importing in general: checking an import, keeping it as code, and finishing one that is incomplete.
